column1: > Where the tunnels land, and how many nodes are on the far side.
> One row per configuration. Columns, tab separated:
>   name       what to call the row, and the cluster it runs on
>   endpoints  which nodes terminate a tunnel, by role: control-plane,
>              worker, worker2, a comma separated list of those, or all
>   remotes    how many provisioned nodes to join over the tunnel
>   cni        the network to install
> Roles rather than node names, so a row says nothing about the cluster
> it runs on and every row can run on its own.
> Every row expects total reachability: each pod reaching every other
> pod and every service, in both directions, whether or not the nodes
> involved terminate a tunnel. A node with no tunnel reaches a remote
> by transiting one that has one, so tunnel placement is meant to be
> invisible from the pod network. Any row that fails is that claim
> being wrong.
